title: Homogenization, multiscale FEM and heterogeneous media

items.title: Uniformly elliptic periodic scalar diffusion data
items.statement:
Fix an integer $d\ge1$ and the unit cell $Y=(0,1)^d$ with Lebesgue measure $|Y|=1$. Assume Countable Choice for the $L^2$ conventions of [[def-countable-choice]]. A **uniformly elliptic periodic scalar diffusion coefficient** is a measurable real function $a:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ such that $a(y+k)=a(y)$ for almost every $y$ and every $k\in\mathbb Z^d$, and there are constants $0<\lambda\le\Lambda<\infty$ with $\lambda\le a(y)\le\Lambda$ almost everywhere on $Y$. Coefficients are identified when they agree almost everywhere.

For $\epsilon>0$, the physical scalar coefficient is $a_\epsilon(x)=a(x/\epsilon)$ and the associated matrix is $a_\epsilon(x)I_d$. The bounded-domain branch used on this page is $\Omega=(0,1)^d$ with homogeneous zero boundary values. Its weak equation for datum $f\in L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ is
$$\int_\Omega a(x/\epsilon)\nabla u_\epsilon\cdot\nabla v\,dx=\int_\Omega fv\,dx\qquad(v\in H^1_0(\Omega;\mathbb R)).$$
No coefficient regularity beyond measurability and the displayed bounds is part of this definition.

For every $\epsilon>0$, the map $x\mapsto x/\epsilon$ is a $C^1$ diffeomorphism of $\mathbb R^d$. By [[thm-c-one-change-of-variables-for-nonnegative-lebesgue-measurable-functions]], its pullback preserves Lebesgue measurability and takes null-set changes to null-set changes (apply the theorem also to the inverse map). Thus $a_\epsilon$ is a well-defined almost-everywhere class independent of the representative of $a$. The same result applies to every affine translation and positive dilation used in periodic sampling below, so almost-everywhere coefficient bounds are preserved under those pullbacks.

The ellipticity bounds hold almost everywhere on all of $\mathbb R^d$, not just on $Y$: periodicity transfers the exceptional null set from $Y$ to each lattice translate, translations preserve null sets by the same change-of-variables theorem, and the countably many translates cover $\mathbb R^d$ up to their null boundaries.
items.strategy: State the coefficient, cell, period, energy form, and weak boundary-value branch.

items.title: Separable H1-zero space and compact L2 inclusion on a cube
items.statement: For the unit cube, H1-zero is a separable Hilbert space, satisfies a choice-free coordinate Poincare bound under countable choice, and is compactly embedded in L2 by Fourier-tail control.
items.strategy: Embed in a finite product of separable L2 spaces, prove Poincare on test functions, and use periodic Fourier coefficients of zero extensions with a uniform high-frequency tail bound.

items.title: Mean-zero Poincare inequality on the periodic cell
items.statement: On the unit cell, each mean-zero periodic H1 function obeys ||v||L2<=sqrt(d)||grad v||L2, and every periodic H1 gradient has zero cell mean.
items.strategy: Prove the zero mean of smooth periodic derivatives on opposite faces, then prove Poincare by coordinate telescoping, Jensen, Fubini, and Cauchy-Schwarz; pass both claims to the closure.

items.title: Periodic averaging and rescaling bounds on the unit cube
items.statement: For periodic L1 data and compactly supported smooth slow factors, cell rescaling converges to the cell mean; periodic L2 rescalings have a uniform L2 bound on the unit cube.
items.strategy: Tile the support by epsilon-cells, compare the slow factor on each cell, bound the boundary-cell remainder, and extend the weak limit by L2 density.

items.statement: For every p in R^d the cell equation has a unique mean-zero solution chi_p, linear in p, with an energy bound depending only on lambda and Lambda.

items.title: Periodic FE-HMM with simplicial macro and periodic P1 micro meshes
items.statement:
This procedure defines a real-arithmetic finite-dimensional FE-HMM discretization. It makes no bit-complexity claim, no coefficient-oracle claim, and no claim about numerically computing its exact integral entries; those entries are the mathematical values of the displayed integrals. Fix $Q=(0,1)^2$ and coefficient $a$ from [[def-periodic-scalar-diffusion-data]]. Use the diagonal of the square from $(0,0)$ to $(1,1)$ as a two-triangle initial matching macro mesh. Label that shared diagonal $0$ in both triangles and each exterior edge $1$. It is a compatible labeled mesh in the sense of [[def-afem-nvb-labelled-triangulation-family]]. The macro input is any finite admissible descendant triangulation $\mathcal T$ of this mesh. Its cells are closed affine triangles as in [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]].

Choose $\epsilon>0$, a micro side length $\delta>0$, $f\in L^2(Q)$, and a finite matching triangulation $\mathcal M$ of the unit square whose opposite boundary edges and vertices match under translation by $e_1,e_2$. The periodic micro space is
$$W_{\mathcal M}:=\{z\in V_\#:z\text{ is continuous and affine on every triangle of }\mathcal M\}.$$
It is a finite-dimensional subspace of $V_\#$; the periodic closure condition identifies opposite traces. Let $V_H$ be the conforming zero-boundary continuous piecewise-affine macro space on $\mathcal T$, using [[def-broken-and-conforming-polynomial-spaces]]. Its inclusion in $H^1_0(Q)$ is supplied by [[thm-matching-continuous-piecewise-polynomials-are-wkp]] and [[thm-zero-boundary-piecewise-polynomials-in-w10p]].

Identify vertices of $\mathcal M$ that match under the opposite-edge translations, and order the resulting periodic vertex classes by the lexicographically least representative of each class. Let $\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_N$ be the continuous periodic P1 nodal functions for these classes, with $\phi_i=1$ at class $i$ and $0$ at the other classes. Set $m_i=\int_Y\phi_i\,dy$. If $N=1$, use the empty basis of $W_{\mathcal M}$; otherwise use
$$\psi_i:=\phi_i-\frac{m_i}{m_1}\phi_1\qquad(2\le i\le N)$$
as the ordered basis of $W_{\mathcal M}$. The nodal basis spans the full periodic P1 space, and these functions form a basis of its mean-zero subspace.

Use the following exact solver on the systems assembled below. Given a real matrix $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ and $b\in\mathbb R^n$, `ExactSolve(A,b)` returns the empty vector if $n=0$. Otherwise form the augmented matrix $[A\mid b]$. For $k=1,\ldots,n$, choose the least row index $p\ge k$ whose current entry in column $k$ is nonzero; if there is no such row, return `singular-system`. Swap rows $p$ and $k$. For each $i=k+1,\ldots,n$, set $r=A_{ik}/A_{kk}$, replace augmented row $i$ by row $i-r\,\mathrm{row}_k$, and set its column-$k$ entry to zero. After this loop, compute $x_n,x_{n-1},\ldots,x_1$ by backward substitution in the resulting upper-triangular system and return $x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$. All arithmetic and zero tests are exact over $\mathbb R$; the systems assembled below are positive definite.

Order macro triangles by lexicographic order of their barycenters. For each such $K$, use its barycenter $x_K$ as the single quadrature point with positive weight $|K|$, and set
$$b_K(y):=a\!\left(\frac{x_K}{\epsilon}+\frac{\delta}{\epsilon}y\right)\quad(y\in Y).$$
The affine change-of-variables theorem [[thm-c-one-change-of-variables-for-nonnegative-lebesgue-measurable-functions]] makes this a measurable coefficient class independent of the representative of $a$, with $\lambda\le b_K\le\Lambda$ almost everywhere. For each coordinate vector $e_j$, in order $j=1,2$, assemble
$$G^K_{i\ell}:=\int_Yb_K\nabla\psi_\ell\cdot\nabla\psi_i\,dy,\qquad r^K_{i,j}:=-\int_Yb_K e_j\cdot\nabla\psi_i\,dy$$
over the micro-basis indices $2\le i,\ell\le N$. If that basis is empty, set $w^h_{K,j}=0$; otherwise call `ExactSolve(G^K,r^K_{\cdot,j})`, index its returned coordinates by $2,\ldots,N$, and set $w^h_{K,j}=\sum_{\ell=2}^N x_\ell\psi_\ell$. Then set
$$A^h_Ke_j:=\int_Yb_K(y)(e_j+\nabla_yw^h_{K,j}(y))\,dy.$$
The `singular-system` branch is included to make the solver instruction total; [[lem-fehmm-micro-cell-solves-wellposedness]] proves it is not reached for these micro systems.

Order the interior vertices of $\mathcal T$ lexicographically and let $\varphi_1,\ldots,\varphi_M$ be the corresponding nodal basis of $V_H$. If $M=0$, set $U_H=0$. Otherwise assemble
$$H_{rs}:=\sum_{K\in\mathcal T}|K|\,\nabla\varphi_s|_K\cdot A^h_K\nabla\varphi_r|_K,\qquad F_r:=\int_Qf\varphi_r\,dx,$$
call `ExactSolve(H,F)`, and set $U_H:=\sum_{s=1}^M x_s\varphi_s$. This basis system is exactly the variational system
$$B_H(U,V)=\sum_{K\in\mathcal T}|K|\,\nabla U|_K\cdot A^h_K\nabla V|_K=\int_QfV\qquad(V\in V_H).$$
The macro matrix is positive definite and its `singular-system` branch is unreachable by [[lem-fehmm-micro-cell-solves-wellposedness]]. Output $U_H$. The centroid quadrature is positive and exact for constants, which is the only quadrature property used in the error theorem.

items.title: No sampling resonance for period-aligned periodic micro cells
items.statement: If the micro sample length is an integer multiple of epsilon and is aligned to a periodic cell phase, the exact periodic-coupling sampled tensor equals A* in every dimension.
items.strategy: Pull the corrector back by the integer dilation, verify its weak cell equation, and average the periodic flux over the integer number of cells.

items.title: One-dimensional nonaligned micro sampling resonance bound
items.statement: For one-dimensional scalar periodic data and periodic coupling on a sample ratio r=delta/epsilon>=1, the exact sampled harmonic tensor differs from A* by at most 2 Lambda^2/lambda times epsilon/delta.
items.strategy: Use the harmonic-mean cell formula, split the interval into whole periods and one remainder, then compare reciprocal averages.

items.title: Periodic scalar Dirichlet homogenization on the unit cube
items.statement: For every bounded periodic scalar coefficient a and f in L2 on the unit cube, the exact H1-zero solutions converge weakly to the unique solution with coefficient A*.
items.strategy: Obtain the two-scale gradient limit, identify the cell equation using epsilon-scaled oscillating tests, average the flux, and use uniqueness to remove subsequences.

items.title: Antisymmetric periodic flux potential
items.statement: Each mean-zero divergence-free periodic corrector flux has an L2 antisymmetric potential whose periodic divergence is the flux and whose norm is bounded by the flux L2 norm.
items.strategy: Solve a mean-zero periodic Poisson problem by Lax-Milgram; prove the vector-potential divergence vanishes by Fourier coefficients.

items.title: Well-posedness of the finite FE-HMM micro solves
items.statement:
For every macro cell $K$ in [[alg-fehmm-periodic-cell-micro-macro]], the coefficient $b_K$ satisfies $\lambda\le b_K\le\Lambda$. For each $p\in\mathbb R^2$, both the full cell problem on $V_\#$ and its restriction to $W_{\mathcal M}$ have unique solutions $w_{K,p}$ and $w^h_{K,p}$. The tensors
$$A_K^{\rm ex}p=\int_Yb_K(p+\nabla w_{K,p}),\qquad A_K^hp=\int_Yb_K(p+\nabla w^h_{K,p})$$
are symmetric and satisfy $\lambda I\le A_K^{\rm ex},A_K^h\le\Lambda I$. Consequently the macro FE-HMM system in the algorithm has a unique solution. The exact Gaussian-elimination calls specified there terminate without the `singular-system` branch and return the unique solutions of the assembled micro and macro variational systems.
items.strategy: Restrict the uniformly elliptic form to the finite periodic subspace and apply Lax-Milgram.

items.title: Strong L2 convergence in periodic Dirichlet homogenization
items.statement: The periodic Dirichlet solutions from the preceding theorem converge strongly in L2 to the homogenized solution.
items.strategy: Apply the local cube compactness lemma to every parameter sequence and identify every strong cluster limit by the weak homogenization theorem.

items.title: Boundary-cutoff corrector estimate for regular periodic data
items.statement: If the cell corrector gradients are bounded and u0 is C2 on the closed cube, a boundary-cutoff first-order corrector approximates u_epsilon in H1 seminorm within C sqrt(epsilon), and u_epsilon-u0 is O(sqrt(epsilon)) in L2.
items.strategy: Construct the cutoff expansion, bound its boundary-strip residual, use the antisymmetric flux potential to gain epsilon in the interior, and test the residual equation with the error.

references.title: Grégoire Allaire, Introduction to Homogenization Theory, Lecture 1
references.locator: §1.3.2, Theorem 1.3.6 and equations (1.48)–(1.50), PDF pp. 17–19: gradient decomposition and homogenized-limit context; the quantitative cutoff estimate is proved locally here.

references.locator: Chapter 2 §§2.1–2.2, printed pp. 26–33: flux-corrector Proposition 2.1.1 and cutoff two-scale expansion with an $O(\epsilon^{1/2})$ H1 estimate in Theorem 2.2.2. Its smoothed expansion differs from this local scalar estimate.

items.title: Energy identity for FE-HMM micro tensor error
items.statement: The discrete cell energy exceeds the exact sampled tensor energy by the squared coefficient-weighted gradient error, giving a bound by the best micro-space approximation of the exact corrector.
items.strategy: Subtract the continuous and discrete variational equations and use the energy-minimizing characterization.

references.locator: §§2–3: cell sampling and the FE-HMM macro/micro error split.

items.title: FE-HMM macro, micro, and sampling error separation
items.statement: If the total micro-plus-sampling tensor discrepancy is below lambda, the FE-HMM macro solution exists uniquely and its energy error is bounded by the best macro approximation plus explicit micro and resonance terms.
items.strategy: Bound the bilinear-form perturbation by the tensor discrepancy, prove coercivity, and derive a finite-dimensional energy-Strang estimate.

references.title: Patrick Ciarlet Jr. and Christian Stohrer, Finite-element heterogeneous multiscale method for the Helmholtz equation
references.locator: §3: discrete macro problem, sampled effective matrices, and micro/macro error terms.

title: Homogenization, multiscale FEM and heterogeneous media — Examples

items.title: Layered medium: harmonic normal and arithmetic tangential means
items.statement: For a two-phase coefficient layered in y1, compute the exact diagonal effective tensor and verify the harmonic/arithmetic directions.
items.strategy: Solve the one-dimensional normal flux equation and test the tangential cell equation directly.

items.title: High contrast destroys contrast-independent conditioning
items.statement: For a layered coefficient taking values kappa and 1 on equal fractions, compute the condition number of A* and show it diverges as kappa decreases to zero.
items.strategy: Use the exact layered tensor from the cell formulas and compute its two eigenvalues.

items.title: A nonaligned one-dimensional micro window has resonance error
items.statement: Compute the exact sampled and homogenized harmonic means for a two-phase periodic coefficient at delta/epsilon=3/2 and verify the resonance bound.
items.strategy: Integrate the reciprocal coefficient over one and one-half periods and compare the two reciprocal averages.

items.title: FE-HMM energy error ledger with distinct components
items.statement: Substitute exact rational macro, micro, resonance, ellipticity, and solution-norm values into the proven FE-HMM error bound.
items.strategy: Compute the discrepancy threshold, coercivity factor, and each error contribution exactly.
